doc.title: Willie J. Humphrey and Willie E. Humphrey Interview, 1959-03-15
doc.interviewee: Willie J. Humphrey and Willie E. Humphrey

title: WPA band, the Mills Blue Rhythm tour and the Edith Wilson package show
summary: He joins the WPA band, then a New York band recording and touring Texas and Pittsburgh with a package show, then short engagements.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: In those days, a lot of the musicians were in that WPA band.

Well, yeah, when I was in the band, I got in the band after that. After that, I had to do something. Any of your brothers in it too? No, no, none of them. I was the only one. And it looked like I wasn't going to be able to get in. They looked like they tried to keep me out of it a long time. Then that's when I left the WPA, and I got a call with the Millsboro Rhythm. And I worked around there, I guess, about six months.
Around New York, or where did you go?
Yeah, yeah, I went to New York. I went to Washington, D.C. I went to New York, and I made records, and a good bit of records, actually.
I might even have heard you in those days, and didn't know you were in the band. I didn't know who the musicians were. Yeah, yeah.

Nice to hear that. I made a trip out of New York, clean down through Texas. We had a package, played all the theaters, all the shows in Texas, all through Texas. Of course, San Antonio played. Went back, and the weather was kind of bad. We were supposed to go back in some place in Pennsylvania. We played, what's that, some theater in Pittsburgh we played. I can't forget the name of it.
Is it out on Wiley Avenue or downtown?
No, it's a big theater downtown. Downtown. I can't think of it. I can't think of it.
The one that had the good bands, I heard Tats Waller out of it.

Well, it must be the bands where all the bands go. We had a package. We had a real good show. We had Pops and, we had Stanley. Stanley, that's what, yeah, Stanley. Pops and Lloyd, we had, we had these two comedians, they were very good. Bud Williams or Bud something, and Boyd, Bud and Boyd I believe they called themselves. And they were good. Remember Bucking Bubbles? No, no, it wasn't Bucking Bubbles. We had this girl, this woman here, some Wilson. She was a singer. Edith Wilson? Edith Wilson was on with us. You heard talk about it. Yeah, I never heard, she made records, never heard of her. Yeah, well she was on a package with us. When I came back, when I come back, well then I just started working short bands, you see. I worked with, well time to time I worked with different bands, I played with Pierron, you know. All the bands I substitute, not regular, because they wanted me to Tuxedo bands a long time but I never would join them regular, original Tuxedos. And I played with the Excelsior band, the old Excelsior band, a long time. Until I started going away on the boat, you see, well that disrupted, you see. And after that, well I didn't bother, I was out of the band, see, and got somebody else.
